The name is often given to children who are believed to have exceptional potential or are destined for greatness. Furthermore, Param is a popular name for deities, temples, and spiritual institutions.
data.spiritual_significance: Param has deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. It is a name that represents the ultimate truth and reality. Param is synonymous with Brahman, the eternal and all-pervading consciousness. It is a name that reminds us of our connection to the divine and our spiritual aspirations. In Hinduism, Param is also associated with the idea of being beyond the finite and the temporal. It represents the infinite and the eternal, and is a reminder of our ultimate goal: to transcend the limitations of the physical world and attain spiritual enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: The name Param is derived from the Sanskrit word 'param' which means 'beyond' or 'supreme'. This name was used in ancient Hindu texts and scripts, including the Upanishads and the Bhagavad Gita. In these texts, Param referred to the ultimate reality or the supreme god, beyond the physical world and the senses.

The name Param is also used as a title for various Hindu deities, including Paramesvara (Supreme Lord) and Paramatma (Supreme Self). These deities were considered to be the highest manifestations of god and were worshipped as the ultimate truth and goal of life.
